findings.mechanism: The new write guard decides what may reach an index line by rendering the entry and reading it back through `_LINE_RE` (index.py:99-134). `_LINE_RE` is indifferent to backslashes, so a title like `Fix the \d{4} regex` round-trips and `unrepresentable` returns None. The rendered line is then handed to `pattern.sub(section, text, count=1)` at render.py:92 as a replacement *template*, where Python expands escapes: I verified with verbatim copies of both patterns (index.py:52-56 and render.py:21-25) that `\d` raises `re.PatternError: bad escape`, `\g<id>` raises IndexError, and `\n`/`\t` are silently turned into a real line break or tab. TestRoundTrip (tests/test_v2_ops.py:894-920) covers `]`, `)` and an embedded newline only, so the second consumer of the line, with the stricter constraint, is untested. The exposure is new in this PR even though the `sub` call is not: next_steps_body now renders the top five of the todo list (render.py:45-55), where before a todo reached the README only if someone called the removed `set_window`, so every added todo now goes through this replacement.
findings.failure_scenario: `add_todo(title=r"Fix the \d{4} regex", link="./s.md")` passes the guard, `idx.write` persists the line at ops.py:377, and `render.render` raises at ops.py:378. The tool returns an exception with the todo already in the index and the README stale. Worse, it is persistent: every later write tool on that thread (retire_todo, set_todo_state, order_todos, log_decision, save_session, index_file) ends in `render.render`, which re-reads the poisoned line and raises again, so the thread is unwritable until someone hand-edits todos-index.md, which SKILL.md says never happens. A title containing `\n` or `\t` does not raise at all: it injects a real break into the README, so the README and the index disagree about the todo and the next render leaves the orphaned half behind as stray text.
findings.fix: Add a parametrized case to TestRoundTrip over `[r"Fix the \d{4} regex", r"Escape the \n here", r"see \g<id>", r"C:\temp\x"]`: call add_todo, then assert the call did not raise, the README contains the title verbatim, and a second add_todo on the same thread still succeeds (that last assertion is what catches the bricking). The repo already treats a backslash as a realistic input at tests/test_v2_ops.py:618-624. The code fix the test should drive is a function replacement at render.py:92, `pattern.sub(lambda _: section, text, count=1)`, which bypasses template expansion entirely; refusing backslashes in `unrepresentable` would be the wrong fix, since the line reads back fine.

findings.mechanism: Two gaps in one loop. (a) `test_a_todo_list_is_not_expected_in_date_order` (tests/test_migrate.py:184-193) asserts only `"out_of_date_order" not in ...`, i.e. it pins the half that is skipped and nothing pins the half that must still run. The dangling check sits above the `continue` (migrate.py:152-154) and no test exercises it for todos: the only dangling test, tests/test_migrate.py:163-168, uses artifacts. Moving the `continue` to the top of the loop body, which the comment's wording invites since it reads as a blanket exemption for todos, silently turns off dangling detection for the todos index with the suite still green. (b) The same loop resolves every todo link as `converted / entry.link.lstrip("./")`, and this PR makes an `http(s)` URL a documented, first-class todo link (ops.py:351, and the add_todo docstring in mcp_server.py: "an external URL when there is an issue or PR"). `Path(converted) / "https://github.com/o/r/issues/16"` never exists, so such a todo is reported as dangling. No test covers a URL link through the audit.
findings.failure_scenario: A thread migrated exactly as skills/threads/v2/migrate-from-v1.md instructs, whose v1 Next steps included "reply on issue #16" and so carries a todo linked to the issue URL, audits as `{"clean": false, "dangling": {"todos": ["https://github.com/..."]}}`. That is a gate firing on a correct migration, which is the exact failure the comment added at migrate.py:156-159 is written to avoid. The other half: a genuine todo pointing at a `./todos/x.md` that was never written goes unreported the moment anyone tidies the `continue` upward.
findings.fix: Two tests in TestAudit. First, write a todos index with `idx.Entry("20260101-a", "active", "A", "./todos/never-written.md")` and assert `json.loads(audit(...))["dangling"]["todos"]` names it; that is the break-the-guard counterpart and it passes today, so it only has to be written down. Second, write one todo linked to an existing `./todos/x.md` and one linked to `https://example.com/i/1` and assert `"dangling" not in` the reply; that one fails today and the fix is to skip a link whose scheme is http(s) in the dangling check.

findings.mechanism: For an indexed file the link is derived from the filename rather than from caller prose, so the realistic breaker is a filename holding `)` or `]`: `Screenshot (1).png`, `report (final).pdf`, names macOS and browsers produce by default. Every UNREPRESENTABLE test is on a todo (title at tests/test_v2_ops.py:171, URL at 181) or an artifact description (897). None uses a filename, and none goes through index_directory, even though mcp_server.py:384 documents `UNREPRESENTABLE - the filename carries a character an index line cannot hold ... Rename the file.` as part of that tool's contract. The guard at ops.py:213-214 does sit before `idx.add`, so behaviour is right today; the ordering is simply unpinned on the bulk path, where the PR's own migration story (sixty-six files in one call) makes it most likely to be hit.
findings.failure_scenario: If the check were moved below `idx.add` (or a later kind routed around it), indexing `./artifacts/Screenshot (1).png` writes `- 19700101-screenshot-1:current [19700101-screenshot-1](./artifacts/Screenshot (1).png)`. `_LINE_RE`'s `[^)]*` stops at the first `)` and the trailing `.png)` fails the tail, so the whole line stops matching: the artifact vanishes from `idx.read` with no error, and the next write of that index erases the line for good. That is the precise loss the new guard exists to prevent, reached on a directory the user never inspected file by file.
findings.fix: In TestIndexDirectory, create `./artifacts/Screenshot (1).png` beside a well-named file. Assert `index_file` on it returns `UNREPRESENTABLE` with `"link"` in the detail and leaves `idx.read(d, "artifacts")` empty, and that `index_directory` reports it under `refused["UNREPRESENTABLE"]` while still indexing the neighbour, mirroring the shape of `test_a_refusal_reports_and_does_not_stop_the_rest`.

findings.mechanism: `ORDERED` declares that nothing may re-sort a todo list and argues in prose that `idx.add` is never involved for a live one. Nothing tests that. `add` (index.py:220-236) still accepts `kind="todos", retired=False` and will date-sort the entire list, it is an ordinary public function, and the tests themselves call it that way for live todos (tests/test_schema_v2.py:288-290 and 384). The grep I ran over `lib/` confirms production code is currently clean (ops.py:137 and 215 only ever see sessions/decisions/artifacts, session.py:44 sessions), so this is a guard gap rather than a live bug, and the repo's own convention is to pin exactly this kind of invariant with an AST test (tests/test_layering.py:169-198).
findings.failure_scenario: A future operation, or a migration helper, appends a todo with `idx.add(thread.dir, "todos", entry)` instead of the read/insert/write at ops.py:358-377. Every user-set priority order in every workspace silently becomes date order on the next add, Next steps shows the five oldest todos rather than the five chosen, and nothing reports anything. AGENTS.md records this class of failure from experience: "That exact pattern shipped once and sorted every workspace alphabetically without complaining."
findings.fix: Add a layering guard in the style of `_dispatched_operations`: walk `lib/ai_workspace/**/*.py` with ast and assert no `idx.add(...)`/`index.add(...)` call passes a literal in `idx.ORDERED` as `kind` without `retired=True`. Stronger and cheaper to keep honest: make `add` raise when `kind in ORDERED and not retired`, and assert that with `pytest.raises` plus one test that `add(..., retired=True)` still lands a retired todo in date order (tests/test_schema_v2.py:160-171 already covers the accepted side).

findings.mechanism: The amend path is separate code from the create path and is unexercised. The only test of a rejected amendment, `test_the_refusal_leaves_the_previous_description_intact` (tests/test_v2_ops.py:737-746), trips the length cap, which returns at ops.py:169-170 before any entry is touched. The UNREPRESENTABLE branch instead mutates `entry.description` in place, discovers the line will not read back, restores `was`, and returns, and nothing covers it. Related and also uncovered: index.py:131-134's fallback, reached when two fields are broken at once (a todo titled `Fix [the] parser` linked to `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merge_(SQL)` is both), returns "the line it makes cannot be read back" and names no field, which contradicts the add_todo docstring's promise that `detail` names the field to reword.
findings.failure_scenario: A reordering of ops.py:188-191 that writes before checking would put an unparseable line into artifacts-index.md while amending a description, losing the entry on the next read; nothing fails. And a caller that hits the two-broken-fields case is told only that the line cannot be read back, so the model has no field to fix and will most likely retry the same values.
findings.fix: Two small tests. Index an artifact with a good description, re-index it with `"one\ntwo"`, and assert `UNREPRESENTABLE`, the stored description unchanged, and `idx.index_path(d, "artifacts").read_text()` byte-identical to before the call. Then one `add_todo(title="Fix [the] parser", link="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merge_(SQL)")` asserting the detail still names a field, which fails today and is fixed by naming the first broken field found rather than falling through.

findings.mechanism:
`test_readme_always_equals_the_projection` claims the README's section always equals `render.next_steps_body(d)`, but it reads the section as `split("## Next steps

")[1].split("

")[0]`, i.e. the first paragraph only, and it uses two todos. The body is now two paragraphs whenever anything is hidden, since render.py:49-54 appends `
{hidden} more in [todos](...)` or `
{parked} parked in ...`; with six todos the assertion would fail on its own slicing rather than on a real disagreement. So the invariant is checked only in the case where the PR's new code contributes nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: A change to how the hidden-count tail is composed (dropping it, or rendering it into the README but not into `next_steps_body` or vice versa) leaves the README and the projection out of step above five todos, and this test, the one that exists to catch exactly that, stays green because it never looks past the first blank line.
findings.fix: Slice the section to the next `^## ` heading instead of the next blank line, and parametrize the test over three states: two active todos, six active todos (exercises the "1 more" tail), and three parked and none active (exercises the "3 parked" tail). Assert the full section equals `next_steps_body(d)` in each.
